text: In a photoelectric effect experiment a light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is made to fall on the surface of photosensitive material. Now if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled, the number of photo electrons emitted will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The incident frequency is $f=1.5f_{0}$, where $f_{0}$ is the threshold frequency.

After halving, the frequency becomes $\dfrac{f}{2}=0.75f_{0}$, which is below $f_{0}$.

Each photon then carries energy $h(0.75f_{0})<hf_{0}=𝜙$, so no photon can eject an electron; doubling the intensity only doubles the number of such photons.

The number of photoelectrons emitted is therefore zero.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: If two vectors $⃗{A}$ and $⃗{B}$ having equal magnitude $R$ are inclined at angle $θ$, then
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For two vectors of equal magnitude $R$ inclined at $θ$:

$|⃗{A}+⃗{B}|^{2}=R^{2}+R^{2}+2R^{2}\cos θ=2R^{2}(1+\cos θ)=4R^{2}\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$

using $1+\cos θ=2\cos ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$. So $|⃗{A}+⃗{B}|=2R\cos \dfrac{θ}{2}$, which matches (A) and rules out (D).

$|⃗{A}-⃗{B}|^{2}=2R^{2}(1-\cos θ)=4R^{2}\sin ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$

using $1-\cos θ=2\sin ^{2}\dfrac{θ}{2}$. So $|⃗{A}-⃗{B}|=2R\sin \dfrac{θ}{2}$, which rules out (B) and (C).

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The speed of sound in oxygen at S.T.P. will be approximately: (given, $R=8.3\mathrm{JK}^{-1},γ=1.4$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At S.T.P., $T=273\text{K}$; for oxygen $M=32\text{g mol}^{-1}=32\times 10^{-3}\text{kg mol}^{-1}$.

Sound travels through a gas as rapid compressions and rarefactions that are adiabatic, so the relevant bulk modulus is $B=γP$ (Laplace correction). With density $ρ=\dfrac{PM}{RT}$ from the ideal gas equation,

$v=\sqrt{\dfrac{γP}{ρ}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{γRT}{M}}$

$v=\sqrt{\dfrac{1.4\times 8.3\times 273}{32\times 10^{-3}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3172.26}{0.032}}=\sqrt{9.91\times 10^{4}}\approx 315\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A gas mixture consists of 8 moles of argon and 6 moles of oxygen at temperature T. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the total internal energy of the gas mixture, we adhere to the equipartition theorem, which dictates that each degree of freedom contributes $\frac{1}{2}RT$ to the internal energy per mole, where $R$ is the gas constant and $T$ is the temperature.

An argon atom, being a noble gas, is monoatomic, with 3 translational degrees of freedom. Since we neglect all vibrational modes, and monoatomic gases have no rotational or vibrational degrees of freedom that contribute to energy at our specified temperature, each mole of argon has $3\times \frac{1}{2}RT=\frac{3}{2}RT$ of energy.

Oxygen, on the other hand, is a diatomic molecule. This implies that under normal conditions, it has 3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom. So, each mole of oxygen has $5\times \frac{1}{2}RT=\frac{5}{2}RT$ of energy as we are neglecting vibrational modes which typically become relevant only at higher temperatures.

Hence, the total internal energy ($U$) of the gas mixture is:

$U=(\text{Energy per mole of Ar}\times \text{Number of moles of Ar})+(\text{Energy per mole of O}_{2}\times \text{Number of moles of O}_{2})$

$U=\left (\frac{3}{2}RT\times 8\right )+\left (\frac{5}{2}RT\times 6\right )$

$U=(12RT+15RT)$

$U=27RT$

Thus, the total internal energy of the system is $27RT$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: A small spherical ball of radius $r$, falling through a viscous medium of negligible density has terminal velocity '$v$'. Another ball of the same mass but of radius $2r$, falling through the same viscous medium will have terminal velocity:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The medium's density is negligible, so buoyancy is negligible and at terminal velocity the weight balances the viscous drag (Stokes' law):

$mg=6πηrv\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{mg}{6πηr}$

Both balls have the same mass $m$, so $v\propto \dfrac{1}{r}$. The relation $v\propto r^{2}$ from $v=\dfrac{2r^{2}ρg}{9η}$ holds only for balls of the same density; at the same mass, doubling $r$ makes the density one-eighth.

$\dfrac{v^{'}}{v}=\dfrac{r}{2r}=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow v^{'}=\dfrac{v}{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text: The resistance per centimeter of a meter bridge wire is $r$, with $X\Omega$ resistance in left gap. Balancing length from left end is at $40\mathrm{cm}$ with $25\Omega$ resistance in right gap. Now the wire is replaced by another wire of $2r$ resistance per centimeter. The new balancing length for same settings will be at
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At balance, the ratio of the gap resistances equals the ratio of the resistances of the two wire segments. With resistance $r$ per cm and balancing length $40\text{cm}$ from the left end:

$\dfrac{X}{25}=\dfrac{r\times 40}{r\times 60}=\dfrac{2}{3}$

With the new wire of resistance $2r$ per cm and new balancing length $\ell$:

$\dfrac{X}{25}=\dfrac{2r\quad \ell }{2r\quad (100-\ell )}=\dfrac{\ell }{100-\ell }$

The resistance per centimetre cancels, so $\dfrac{\ell }{100-\ell }=\dfrac{2}{3}\Rightarrow \ell =40\text{cm}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Light from a point source in air falls on a convex curved surface of radius $20\mathrm{cm}$ and refractive index 1.5. If the source is located at $100\mathrm{cm}$ from the convex surface, the image will be formed at $________$ $\mathrm{cm}$ from the object.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the problem, you're dealing with refraction at a convex surface. The light is coming from a point source located in air (with a refractive index, $μ_{1}=1.0$) and entering a medium with a refractive index of $μ_{2}=1.5$. The convex surface has a radius of curvature $R=20\text{cm}$, and the source is placed $100\text{cm}$ from the convex surface.

The formula used to find the image distance $v$ due to refraction at a spherical surface is:

$\frac{μ_{2}}{v}-\frac{μ_{1}}{u}=\frac{μ_{2}-μ_{1}}{R}$

Substituting the given values:

$\frac{1.5}{v}-\frac{1}{-100}=\frac{1.5-1}{20}$

This equation allows us to solve for $v$, the distance from the convex surface to the image. Upon solving, we found that $v=100\text{cm}$, which means the image forms $100\text{cm}$ on the other side of the convex surface, away from the point of refraction.

The distance from the object to the image isn't just $v$, the distance from the surface to where the image forms. Since the object is $100\text{cm}$ from the convex surface and the image also forms $100\text{cm}$ from the convex surface but on the opposite side, the total distance between the object and the image is the sum of these distances:

Distance from the object to the convex surface: $100\text{cm}$
Distance from the convex surface to the image: $100\text{cm}$

Therefore, the total distance between the object and the image is $100\text{cm}+100\text{cm}=200\text{cm}$.

This calculation accounts for the physical layout where the object and the image are on opposite sides of the convex surface, and to determine the distance between them, you sum the distances from each to the surface. This results in the image being formed $200\text{cm}$ from the object, which means if you were to measure directly from the object to its image, the total distance covered would be $200\text{cm}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift

text:
The distance between charges $+q$ and $-q$ is $2l$ and between $+2q$ and $-2q$ is $4l$. The electrostatic potential at point $P$ at a distance $r$ from center $O$ is $-α\left [\frac{ql}{r^{2}}\right ]\times 10^{9}\mathrm{V}$, where the value of $α$ is $__________. ($Use $\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}\mathrm{Nm}^{2}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Charges $-q$ and $+q$, a distance $2l$ apart, form a dipole $p_{1}=q(2l)=2ql$ pointing from $-q$ to $+q$, that is, to the right of O.

Charges $+2q$ and $-2q$, a distance $4l$ apart, form a dipole $p_{2}=2q(4l)=8ql$ pointing from $-2q$ to $+2q$, that is, to the left of O.

Both dipoles are centred at O, so for $r\gg l$ the system acts as one dipole of moment $p=8ql-2ql=6ql$ pointing to the left. OP makes $60^{\circ }$ with the line on the right, so the angle between $⃗{p}$ and $OP\leftarrow$ is $θ=180^{\circ }-60^{\circ }=120^{\circ }$.

$V=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\frac{p\cos θ}{r^{2}}=\frac{9\times 10^{9}\times 6ql\times \cos 120^{\circ }}{r^{2}}=-27\left [\frac{ql}{r^{2}}\right ]\times 10^{9}\text{V}$

Hence, the answer is 27.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 31st January Evening Shift
